newsitem.title: LATVIA: World Bank says Latvia reform progress good.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says Latvia reform progress good.

text.p: A World Bank mission to Latvia said on Friday that it was satisfied with the country's progress in bringing sustainable economic growth.
The mission has been examining Latvia's performance under the terms of a $60 million structural adjustment loan.

"Latvia has been successful in stabilising its economy and the progress in the structural reform area has been good," World Bank economist and head of the mission, Mansour Farsad, told a news conference.
"Latvia is beginning to show signs of growth, with its GDP projected to increase to four percent in 1997," he added.
But he said that reforms of the state administration and education financing were among the areas where progress was slow but the first steps have already been made.
He said the aim of the structural adjustment loan was to maintain sustainable growth.

The government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele has economic reform among its top priorities. It plans to complete privatisation by mid-1998 and is trying to implement fiscal austerity with balanced budgets this year and next.
Farsad said the World Bank was satisfied with the reduction in energy payment arrears to Latvenergo and Latvian gas.
"Payment of (utility) bills is close to international norms now," Farsad said.
Arrears have been reduced from 200 days a year ago to 30 days for Latvenergo, the electricity firm, and 40 days for gas monopoly Latvian Gas.
"The planned merging of the social insurance fund and the state revenue service, due by the end of the year, will also reduce the amount of overdue payment," Farsad said.
Farsad said the mission was satisfied with the management of state resources and health sector reform, currently in a first stage.
